title: Grateful Dead Live at Meramec Community College on 1970-05-14
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1970 show with scorching New Speedway/Nobody’s Fault jam and a smoking Lovelight; soundboard source is clear enough to enjoy despite occasional rough edges.
ai_review.review: The May 14, 1970 Washington University concert is remembered for its blistering New Speedway → Nobody's Fault → New Speedway sandwich, a fast‑tempo Lovelight, and standout acoustic moments like Schoolgirl and St. Stephen. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s ferocious guitar and vocals while noting the soundboard recording is generally good—crisp for the era with a few low‑level spots in the acoustic set. Overall the performance shines even if a handful of listeners find the playing merely competent.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen reviews average ~4.4 stars, overwhelmingly positive about both performance and audio; only a few mild criticisms keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and crisp for a 1970 soundboard, with occasional roughness or low levels in the acoustic set; no major drop‑outs reported.

standout_songs: New Speedway Boogie (sandwich with Nobody's Fault)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic opener (Silver Threads, Schoolgirl) leads into a high‑octane electric set highlighted by the New Speedway → Nobody's Fault → New Speedway jam and a fast‑tempo Lovelight finale; the energy builds steadily throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for ferocious guitar tone, gritty vocal delivery, and punching riffs—often described as "on fire" or "nasty".
band_member_comments.Drums: Only one drummer (Bill Kreutzmann) is noted; a few reviewers clarify that Mickey Hart was not playing.
